# Audit instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change
- `head/` — every touched file after the change

Audit the change as the security auditor for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.

Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
---
---
name: "audit-sprint"
version: "1.1.0"
description: |
  Security and quality audit of sprint implementation.
  Final gate before sprint completion. Creates COMPLETED marker on approval.
  Resolves local sprint IDs to global IDs via Sprint Ledger.

arguments:
  - name: "sprint_id"
    type: "string"
    pattern: "^sprint-[0-9]+$"
    required: true
    description: "Sprint to audit (e.g., sprint-1)"
    examples: ["sprint-1", "sprint-2", "sprint-10"]

agent: "auditing-security"
agent_path: "skills/auditing-security/"

context_files:
  - path: "grimoires/loa/prd.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Product requirements for context"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/sdd.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Architecture decisions for alignment"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Sprint tasks and acceptance criteria"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
    required: false
    purpose: "Sprint Ledger for ID resolution"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id/reviewer.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Engineer's implementation report"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id/engineer-feedback.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Senior lead approval verification"

pre_flight:
  - check: "pattern_match"
    value: "$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id"
    pattern: "^sprint-[0-9]+$"
    error: "Invalid sprint ID. Expected format: sprint-N (e.g., sprint-1)"

  - check: "script"
    script: ".claude/scripts/validate-sprint-id.sh"
    args: ["$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id"]
    store_result: "sprint_resolution"
    purpose: "Resolve local sprint ID to global ID via ledger"

  - check: "directory_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID"
    error: "Sprint directory not found. Run /implement $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."

  - check: "file_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/reviewer.md"
    error: "No implementation report found. Run /implement $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."

  - check: "file_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/engineer-feedback.md"
    error: "Sprint has not been reviewed. Run /review-sprint $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."
    # Construct-aware: when a construct declares review: skip, the review gate
    # is bypassed and engineer-feedback.md won't exist. Read .run/construct-workflow.json
    # to evaluate this condition.
    skip_when:
      construct_gate: "review"
      gate_value: "skip"

  - check: "content_contains"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/engineer-feedback.md"
    pattern: "All good"
    error: "Sprint has not been approved by senior lead. Run /review-sprint $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."
    # Construct-aware: when a construct declares review: skip, the "All good"
    # approval check is bypassed. The construct's own workflow gates enforce quality.
    skip_when:
      construct_gate: "review"
      gate_value: "skip"

  - check: "file_not_exists"
---

head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726 — HIGH: `isLocalVoice` (and `applyLocality`, line 739) decides locality from `dispatch_group` alone and ignores the model entry's `fallback_chain`; under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` Bridgebuilder keeps a voice whose local model falls back to a hosted hop, and cheval walks that chain inside the call when the local server fails, so PR content reaches a hosted provider. `hop-locality.py:133` classifies the same entry as hosted for the dissent and Flatline, so the posture's "refuses every hosted hop by name" contract holds for three of four consumers.
head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:26 — MEDIUM: the module promises request-time rules (no proxy env, no redirects, declared path prefix) for every opted-in or `dispatch_group: local` provider, but `TransportPolicy` is constructed only by `OpenAIAdapter._transport_policy` (`openai_adapter.py:217-223`) while `validate_providers` (lines 143-156) accepts `allow_insecure_endpoint` for any non-CLI provider type; a `type: anthropic` provider with an http loopback opt-in loads (reproduced) and its adapter calls `http_post` without `policy`, so proxy env vars are honoured and the urllib fallback follows redirects.
head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1428 — MEDIUM (complexity): `_probe_configured` is ~110 lines with four repeated early-return state blocks; `loadTrustedConfig` (`config.ts:605`, ~100 lines) and `_adv_advisory_block` (`adversarial-review.sh:3972`, ~60 lines with a 30-line embedded jq program) also exceed the 50-line threshold without justification.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116 — LOW: the planner (and Bridgebuilder `config.ts:730-732`) treats a provider-level `dispatch_group: local` or "every declared model is local" as local, but cheval's loader requires `dispatch_group` on every model (`loader.py:643`, reproduced CONFIG-INVALID), reads only the model-level key (`cheval.py:541`) and records `hop_locality` from the model entry alone (`modelinv.py:473-476`); the planner plans a hop cheval then refuses — three definitions of "local".
head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1469 — LOW: `_probe_configured` validates a configured provider's `/models` URL with the host-allowlist pipeline, while cheval admits operator-declared https hosts via `validate_declared_endpoint`; a hosted open-weight API that loads in cheval is answered `UNKNOWN / endpoint_refused` by the probe.
head/README.md:22 — LOW: the implementation report (`pr/PR.md`) carries no AC Verification walkthrough and no record of the TypeScript type-check/`npm test` run; the README points at a CHANGELOG entry that is not in the diff.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). ## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`

Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.

===ENG
# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md (Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff` — sprint-257, cycle-129)
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change is large (80 files) and, on the whole, carefully built: the per-provider insecure-endpoint opt-in is implemented once in the canonical validator and reused by the cheval loader, the bash wrapper and the health probe; the `TransportPolicy` request-time rules (no proxy env, no redirects, declared path prefix) are tested against a real 127.0.0.1 stub on both the httpx and urllib transports; advisory voices are kept byte-for-byte out of the counted envelope; the `local_voices` posture refuses hosted hops by name in the dissent and Flatline through one fail-closed classifier; Bridgebuilder reads provider declarations from trusted configuration only. The new tests are substantive and I ran them: 123 Python tests pass, 45 bats tests pass (one skipped for a missing `prd.md`). Two bats failures seen on a first run were caused by the sandbox's `/tmp` being mounted `noexec`, not by the PR, and pass from an executable path. The Bridgebuilder TypeScript tests could not be run here (no `node_modules`); `dist/.build-manifest.json` hashes match the head sources for every changed `.ts` file.

The verdict turns on one gap in the posture feature: the PR defines "local" three different ways across its four consumers, and the Bridgebuilder definition admits a hop the PR's own classifier refuses. Under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` Bridgebuilder keeps a voice whose local model carries a hosted `fallback_chain`; cheval walks that chain inside the call, so the PR content can reach a hosted provider under a posture whose stated contract is "refuses every hosted hop by name". The dissent and Flatline do not have this hole because `hop-locality.py` classifies such an entry as hosted. One `HIGH` finding forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED` under the one-way rule.

Also noted: the request-time `TransportPolicy` is wired only into the OpenAI adapter while the load-time opt-in is accepted for any provider type (MEDIUM); two LOW consistency gaps; and the implementation report (`pr/PR.md`) carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough. Per `pr/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md` the PR files are the entire input and pre-flight steps that need sprint artifacts are skipped, so the missing walkthrough is recorded as an observation rather than applied as the automatic rule; the verdict here is driven by the code findings.

Testing caveat: the only runnable tree available was the workspace framework (a newer revision than the PR base) with every `pr/head/` file overlaid. All test results above are from that hybrid tree; every finding below was confirmed by reading the `pr/head/` files or by a reproduction against them, not inferred from test output alone.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security posture — Bridgebuilder's locality check diverges from the PR's own classifier

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726-733` — `isLocalVoice` decides locality from `dispatch_group` alone and never looks at the model entry's `fallback_chain`; under `local_voices` a voice whose local model falls back to a hosted hop is kept by `applyLocality` (line 739) and cheval walks the chain to the hosted provider when the local server fails.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726-733` (and `applyLocality`, line 739)
**Issue:** The PR's classifier for the dissent and Flatline, `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:16` and `:133`, states the rule: "every hop on the entry's own `fallback_chain` is local by the same rule — cheval walks that chain inside one call", and returns `hosted` with reason `fallback_chain_reaches_hosted:<hop>` otherwise (pinned by bats LOC-7). Bridgebuilder's `isLocalVoice` has no equivalent: trusted config `hounfour.locality: local_voices`, provider `lan` with model `qwen` `dispatch_group: local`, `fallback_chain: ["openai:gpt-5.5"]`, multi-model voice `lan/qwen` → `applyLocality` keeps the voice; when the local server is down, cheval (which every voice dispatches through, `multi-model-pipeline.ts:225`) walks to `openai:gpt-5.5` and the PR diff leaves the host. `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:181` promises that under `local_voices` "every voice whose provider is not `dispatch_group: local` in the trusted config is dropped … and never rerouted"; the README and `multi-model-reference.md` promise the same across "the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and the probe".
**Why This Matters:** `local_voices` is a confidentiality posture (FR-8). The dissent and Flatline honour the fallback-chain rule; Bridgebuilder does not, so the guarantee holds for three of four consumers and the operator has no way to know which. The same function also admits two shapes cheval's loader rejects outright (see Observation 2), so Bridgebuilder's notion of "local" is neither cheval's nor hop-locality.py's.
**Required Fix:** Give Bridgebuilder the same classification as the shell callers: either (a) have `loadTrustedConfig` parse `models.<id>.fallback_chain` into `ProviderDecl` and make `isLocalVoice` recurse over the chain against the trusted declarations plus the generated registry (hosted when any hop is not local, `MAX_DEPTH`-bounded, unresolved = hosted), or (b) shell out to `hop-locality.py` with the trusted config text. Add a `trusted-config.test.ts` case mirroring bats LOC-7 (`qwen-leaky` with `fallback_chain: ["openai:gpt-5.5"]` is refused with a named reason) and a test that an undeclared fallback hop is treated as hosted.
**Reference:** SDD D-8.1 (plan-time refusal, never rerouted); CWE-200 (exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor) for the posture breach.

---

## Observations

### 1. Request-time rules apply to one adapter type only

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:26` — the module promises "for an opted-in provider, or a model whose `dispatch_group` is `local`, the adapter ignores proxy environment variables, refuses HTTP redirects and requires every request URL to stay under the declared endpoint path", but `TransportPolicy` is constructed only by `OpenAIAdapter._transport_policy` (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:217-223`); `validate_providers` (`endpoint_policy.py:143-156`) accepts `allow_insecure_endpoint` for any non-CLI provider type.
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:217-223`; `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/base.py:270,378,468` (the `policy` keyword is optional and defaults to None)
**Suggestion:** Reproduced: a `type: anthropic` provider with `endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:9100/v1`, `keyless: true`, `allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"` loads cleanly, and the Anthropic and Google adapters call `http_post`/`http_post_stream`/`http_get` without `policy`, so proxy env vars are honoured and the urllib fallback follows redirects for that provider. Either refuse the opt-in and `dispatch_group: local` at load for provider types whose adapter does not implement the policy (fail closed, with a named reason), or move policy construction into `ProviderAdapter` so every adapter type gets it. Add a load test for the refused shape.
**Benefit:** The documented request-time guarantee becomes true for every provider the loader admits, not only `openai`/`openai_compat`.

### 2. Three definitions of "local" for one hop

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116` — the planner (and Bridgebuilder, `config.ts:730-732`) treats a provider-level `dispatch_group: local`, or "every declared model is local", as local, while cheval's loader requires `dispatch_group` on every model entry (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/loader.py:643`, `_validate_model_auth_metadata`: reproduced `CONFIG-INVALID … missing required 'dispatch_group'`), reads only the model-level key into `ModelConfig` (`head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:541`) and records `hop_locality` from the model entry alone (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:473-476`).
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116`; `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:730-732`; `trusted-config.test.ts:359` pins the "every declared model is local" rule for a provider with no models at all
**Suggestion:** A provider-level `dispatch_group` plans a hop cheval then refuses at load, so nothing leaks, but the planners' docstring ("that model entry, or its provider block", `hop-locality.py:15`) describes a config shape the dispatcher never accepts. Drop the provider-block rule from both classifiers (model-level only, matching cheval and D-8.0), or make cheval honour the provider-level key everywhere (loader, `ModelConfig`, `hop_locality_of`, `_transport_policy`). One rule, one place.
**Benefit:** One answer to "is this hop local" across plan time, dispatch and MODELINV.

### 3. The probe applies a different endpoint rule than cheval to configured providers

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1469` — `_probe_configured` validates the configured provider's `/models` URL with the host-allowlist pipeline (`--allowlist "$PROBE_PROVIDERS_ALLOWLIST"`), while cheval admits an operator-declared https host through `validate_declared_endpoint` (no allowlist). A hosted open-weight API such as `https://api.example-inference.com/v1` loads in cheval but is answered `UNKNOWN / endpoint_refused` by the probe.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1469`
**Suggestion:** The docs say the probe goes "through the endpoint rule" as cheval does. Either pass a declared-endpoint mode to the validator CLI for configured providers, or say in the probe's `--help` and `scripts-reference.md` that configured https providers must also be on the probe allowlist. Not silent (the reason is named), hence LOW.
**Benefit:** The probe answers for every provider cheval will dispatch to.

### 4. Report and documentation

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/README.md:22` — the implementation report (`pr/PR.md`, one line plus a file count) carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, no assumptions, and no record of the formatter/type-check self-checks (FAST-GATE: `tsc --noEmit` for the Bridgebuilder sources is not evidenced; the `dist/` hashes do match the sources). The README's "Unreleased — earned guards and open voices" block points at `CHANGELOG.md`, which is not in the diff and could not be checked here.
**Suggestion:** On re-submission include the AC walkthrough with `file:line` + symbol per criterion, the test commands run (the six pytest files, the seven bats files, `npm test` for the skill) and the CHANGELOG entry or a pointer to the commit that carries it.
**Benefit:** Lets the next reviewer verify rather than re-derive.

### 5. Complexity

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1428` — `SIMPLICITY[shrink]`: `_probe_configured` is ~110 lines with four early-return state blocks that repeat the same five assignments; `loadTrustedConfig` (`head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:605`) is ~100 lines and `_adv_advisory_block` (`head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:3972`) ~60 lines with a 30-line embedded jq program. All three exceed the 50-line threshold without a justification comment.
**Suggestion:** In the probe, a `_probe_unknown <reason> <class>` helper removes ~20 lines; in `config.ts`, split the PR-mode source resolution (settings → base ref → main) into its own function; in the shell, move the jq program to a `.jq` file beside the schemas. `net: -60 lines possible`.
**Benefit:** Each unit becomes readable in one screen and testable on its own.

---

## Rejected dissent payloads

None. The envelope's `metadata.rejected_summary` is empty and the named sidecar `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-rejected-review.jsonl` has zero rows (both voices' payloads validated without repair).

---

## Cross-Model Observations

Adversarial review ran on `pr/head.diff` (`grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-review.json`): primary `gpt-5.5-pro` (answered by `codex-headless`), companion `claude-headless`, two independent voices, verdict quality APPROVED, 7 findings. Each was verified against the head files:

- **DISS-001 (BLOCKING, primary)** — "a `dispatch_group: local` provider with an https loopback endpoint and no opt-in gets no TransportPolicy". Refuted: a model-level `dispatch_group: local` does produce a policy (`openai_adapter.py:221`), and a provider-level-only key never loads (cheval requires the model-level key, Observation 2). An https loopback or RFC1918 literal without an opt-in is refused at load (`ENDPOINT-IP-BLOCKED`, pinned by `test_config_examples_load.py`). Not counted.
- **DISS-002 (BLOCKING, primary)** — "the loader does not stop a local model's `fallback_chain` from reaching a hosted provider". Partly confirmed: cheval's loader indeed does not, and the dissent/Flatline planners compensate with `hop-locality.py`; Bridgebuilder does not. Counted as Changes Required 1.
- **DISS-C-001 (ADVISORY, companion)** — provider-level `dispatch_group` diverges between the planner and cheval. Confirmed as a consistency gap, but cheval fails closed at load; counted as Observation 2 (LOW), not as the leak the voice described.
- **DISS-C-002 (ADVISORY)** — `cost-report.sh` would count `stale_catalog` rows as unpriced. Refuted: that script classifies unpriced as `pricing_source == "unknown"` only and buckets by `pricing_resolution`; the budget enforcer likewise keys on `unknown`.
- **DISS-C-003 (ADVISORY)** — the final MODELINV emit derives the hop from `models_failed[-1].model`, which "is very likely a bare id". Refuted: `_entry_target = _entry.canonical` (`provider:model`), and the e2e test's all-hops-failed case asserts `destination.provider == "local"`.
- **DISS-C-004 (ADVISORY)** — TransportPolicy only on OpenAI adapters. Confirmed and reproduced; counted as Observation 1 (MEDIUM).
- **DISS-C-005 (ADVISORY)** — a templated `{region}` catalog endpoint would fail every load. Refuted: `validate_declared_endpoint("https://bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com")` returns valid and the default catalog loads (`test_hosted_defaults_still_load_unchanged`).

---

## Acceptance Criteria Check

### Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff`

| Criterion | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Per-provider insecure-endpoint opt-in: one rule, both paths agree (D-7.2) | Pass | `test_endpoint_validator_optin.py` runs one 30-case table through the validator and `endpoint_policy.check_endpoint`; both agree on code and verdict |

| Thinking traces: `reasoning_content` and leading `<think>` to `thinking`, `thinking_stripped` recorded | Pass | `test_openai_thinking_strip.py`; tracker `on_progress` keeps the first-token deadline alive without feeding content |

===ADVRES
# auditing-security — Security Dissenter (Phase 1C) detail

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:
`payload` is the model's finding as normalised, `reject_reason` the clause it failed, and
`repair_attempted` / `repair_succeeded` whether the bounded repair round-trip ran.

**Round-1 hardening (sprint-248 review, sixteen live two-voice runs).** One list, by envelope field; both skills' copies of
this block are kept byte-identical (CMP-138 fails on any drift).

- **Two voices, one envelope.** The companion runs in its own sub-workdir with a log and its own copies of the prompt files.
  The envelope's `cost_usd` / tokens are BOTH voices; the per-voice spend stays under `companion_voice.cost_cents`, and
  `budget_cents` is a per-voice cap (a malformed cap is 0 cents — the run fails closed with `status: budget_exceeded`).
  Findings carry `voice` (the outer hop, matching `final_model`) and `answered_by` (the model that produced them);
  `companion_voice.answered_by` is the companion's own succeeded id. An operator may set
  `flatline_protocol.<block>.companion_chain: {anthropic: [...], openai: [...]}` to replace the default chains of D-2.1
  (used as given; only those two keys are read — keyed by the companion's family). A family with neither a credential nor its CLI on PATH is `reason: no_route`; a prompt copy that fails
  is `reason: prompt_copy_failed` (no fork). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_KEEP_WORKDIR=1` keeps the `/tmp` workdir's files, never a
  process.
- **`companion_voice.independent` / `counted_as`.** Independence compares the two `answered_by` families (the primary's
  succeeded id, not its configured hop). Same family — or either family `unknown`, an id no catalog entry or name rule
  places, which is no evidence of a second family: the companion's findings are kept (tagged) but its envelope
  contributes no voice to verdict quality — `counted_as: duplicate_voice` (the aggregator counts distinct voices; its
  INV-5 forbids one id both succeeded and dropped, so a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's succeeded voices
  feeds no dropped-voice envelope either, and a MIXED attempt envelope keeps its own voice: a copy without the conflicting
  dropped entry is aggregated — `primary_attempts_rewritten` / `companion_attempts_rewritten`; an envelope with no
  succeeded voice that dropped the other side's voice is excluded — `primary_attempts_excluded` /
  `companion_attempts_excluded`). A primary that never answered leaves the companion `counted_as: sole_voice`
  (`independent: null`). A primary chain that exhausts while the companion completes is promoted (`status: reviewed`,
  `degraded: true`, `primary_voice: {status: failed}`) so the completed voice is never buried. An aggregator failure is
  named on the envelope (`verdict_quality_error`). A fold that fails keeps the primary envelope
  (`companion_voice.status: fold_failed`) and counts the companion as a dropped voice.
- **Shared hops (`companion_voice.shared_hops`, `primary_voice.status: ceded`).** A hop both chains hold (typically the
  other family's CLI as the primary's last resort) stays in the companion chain and is listed under `shared_hops`,
  compared by canonical name (a provider prefix or a catalog alias is the same hop). When the primary reaches a shared hop
  it waits for the companion to settle (bounded by the wait cap) and skips the hop only when the companion ANSWERED with
  it — `model_attempts` records `<hop>:skipped_shared_with_companion` and the envelope says `primary_voice: {status:
  ceded, hop}` with `degraded: false`; a companion that failed the hop, or never reached it, leaves it to the primary; a
  companion still ON the hop past the wait cap is reaped where the primary stands and the primary runs the hop; a
  companion that already answered and is finishing (its post phase) is left to the post budget. The binary is never run
  twice for the same prompt.
- **Rejected rows (`metadata.rejected_summary`, `metadata.rejected_sidecars`).** Every rejected payload lands in a sidecar
  row and in `rejected_summary` (each entry carries the row's `index` and the raw payload's title —
  `title_derived` when only the normaliser's positional id names it; an empty id or title is absent); the companion's
  rows are in its own `-companion.jsonl`, named on the envelope (`companion_voice.rejected_sidecar`, `null` and the file
  removed when nothing was rejected). `verdict-derive.sh` counts the rows of the sidecars the envelope names
  (`rejected_sidecars`): at start the run moves the previous run's envelope and its two sidecars aside (`.prev`) and it
  lists the sidecars it produced; a run that writes its envelope drops the `.prev` files; a run that aborts leaves NO envelope
  at the path and the `.prev` files beside it (the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback);
  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_TAG` scopes the NAMES — `adversarial-rejected-<gate>[-companion][-<tag>].jsonl` — so a chunk driver
  passes its chunk key and nothing is renamed afterwards (a tag outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` becomes a short hash of its
  raw value, said once, so distinct tags never share a file). A non-empty sidecar a listing envelope does not name is never
  silent whatever its age: its rows count toward the section and a warning names the file (newer than the envelope: the
  envelope may be stale — re-run; older: an earlier run's rows that were never folded — triage them or remove the file; a
  chunk driver clears the directory's rejected set at the start of a round). Without an envelope, or without that field,
  every `adversarial-rejected-<gate>*.jsonl` beside the envelope's place counts. A pre-FR-2 envelope (no metadata at all,
  or a metadata without a `rejected_summary` key and without any FR-2 marker — `rejected_sidecars`, `companion_voice`;
  never `rejected_count`, which the writer before cycle-126 set too) counts none of the rows as old as itself, with a
  warning — historical sprints keep their verdicts — but a sidecar NEWER than it counts (one git tracks with its committed
  bytes is history, whatever mtime a checkout gave it). Rows whose repair succeeded
  never count; a trailer-less file is held to the contract too; the same section with one top-level bullet per payload
  clears it in every case.
- **Wait cap and reaping (`failure_class: timeout`).** The second voice is reaped on INT/TERM/EXIT (one cleanup trap for
  the whole run, the whole process tree — re-collected after the freeze and before KILL — TERM then KILL after
  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REAP_GRACE_SECONDS`, the companion's pid trusted only while its start token matches the one recorded at
  the fork) and by a wait cap measured from its start: each `*-headless` hop counts the CLI adapter's bound — connect +
  max(600 s, the catalog's per-model `headless_timeout_seconds`, CLI hops only, capped at 3,600 s when the catalog loads;
  `claude-headless` carries 900 s because a dissent on `claude -p` takes 6–10 minutes; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_CLI_HOP_TIMEOUT` is
  the fallback for a hop no catalog lists; a listed hop without the key is bound by the formula, 610 s) — each HTTP hop `timeout_seconds`, plus its lock wait and the CLI bound when its catalog chain falls through to a CLI
  hop (it takes that binary's lock before its request, as a `queue` phase; cheval walks the chain inside one call), plus
  30 s (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_COMPANION_WAIT_SECONDS` pins it). The deadline follows the companion's phase (queue → hop → post) under a global ceiling; the post-hop work
  (validation, repair round-trips) has its own budget, so a model that answered is never reaped mid-processing; the
  primary's wait on a shared hop applies the same model (a companion in `post` on another hop frees the hop at once; on
  the shared hop the primary waits for the settled record). The previous run's envelope and sidecars are moved aside at
  start (`.prev`) and never restored — see "Rejected rows". Every
  numeric knob (`timeout_seconds`, the context-escalation sizes, the operator seconds) is a whole number
  without a leading zero, or its default applies with a warning — except `budget_cents` / `--budget`, which fail closed
  (0 cents, `status: budget_exceeded`, exit 4).
- **Locks.** `*-headless` hops — the dissent hops, the repair round-trips, and an HTTP alias whose catalog chain falls
  through to a CLI hop — are serialised per CLI binary across the two walks (a per-user flock under
  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`$TMPDIR`, 0700, ours, never a symlink); a lock not acquired within the hop's bound fails that hop as
  `lock_wait` — no request was sent (the chain walks on); a model that merely resolves to a CLI hop, and a repair, wait only their own call
  timeout; queueing for the lock is not charged to the hop's cap; without `flock` (or a lock directory that is not ours)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Security Audit Scope Analysis
# Two-Pass Methodology v1.0
#
# Shows file counts by security-relevant category to understand audit surface.
# Part of Loa's /audit skill enhancement.
#
# Usage: .claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh [OPTIONS]
#   --no-symlinks    Skip symlinks (default: follow)
#   --max-depth N    Limit search depth (default: unlimited)
#   --json           Output as JSON

set -euo pipefail

# Parse arguments
FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=true
MAX_DEPTH=""
OUTPUT_JSON=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case $1 in
    --no-symlinks) FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=false; shift ;;
    --max-depth) MAX_DEPTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) OUTPUT_JSON=true; shift ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# Build find options as array (HIGH-002 remediation - prevents word splitting)
declare -a FIND_OPTS=(-type f)
if [[ "$FOLLOW_SYMLINKS" == "false" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-type f -not -type l)
fi
if [[ -n "$MAX_DEPTH" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-maxdepth "$MAX_DEPTH" "${FIND_OPTS[@]}")
fi

# Exclude patterns (POSIX compatible)
EXCLUDE_DIRS="node_modules|\.git|dist|build|\.next|vendor|__pycache__|\.venv"

# Count function with error suppression
# Uses array expansion for safe variable handling
count_files() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*.ts" -o -name "*.js" -o -name "*.py" -o -name "*.go" -o -name "*.java" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | \
    xargs grep -l "$pattern" 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

count_by_name() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*$pattern*" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

  and a diagnostic saying "timed out" (cheval reports its own CLI-hop timeout as `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`) too; 5
  (`INVALID_RESPONSE`) or a `malformed_response` status `malformed`; anything else (1: API error, provider unavailable,
  token revoked) `model_unavailable`; a hop whose CLI lock was never acquired is `lock_wait` (no request was sent).
  `last_error` is an allowlisted summary of the provider's own line — cheval's error
  tokens, "timed out after Ns", HTTP / exit codes — read from the MODELINV ledger row cheval wrote for the call (the
  model-adapter shim discards cheval's stderr; the row is matched by model, primitive and the window of the companion's
  LAST hop, so a repair on the same model during its post phase is not its row; concurrent dissents on one host could still
  supply each other's line — another reason drivers run sequentially), else from the last non-banner line of the
  companion's log; it also masks bare provider-key shapes (`sk-…`, `xai-…`, `gsk_…`, `AIza…`) the shared redactor does not
  cover. The redacted raw line is printed to stderr and stays in the `/tmp` workdir, removed on exit; the a2a directory
  receives the envelope and the sidecars.

  credential) → `claude-headless` (with the binary on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last, one bounded attempt
  each (by canonical name: a prefixed answering voice is not appended twice); a hop that failed with an explicit auth /
  quota code is retired for the run's remaining repairs, the answering voice never; a repair skips a hop the companion is
  running at that moment (`repair_hops_skipped` names it, once) and waits for a CLI lock only its own timeout (a hop
  whose wait expires never ran: named `<hop>:lock_wait`, once, and no repair slot is spent); the run's
  repairs share a wall-clock budget (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS`, default 5 × timeout × 2 or twice the heaviest hop's charge
  (below) plus a timeout if that is more; a hop whose estimate — twice its last observed duration, at least the timeout,
  at most its bound — exceeds what is left is not started and is named `<hop>:over_budget`; spent, the rest are rejected
  unrepaired and counted in `repair_budget_exhausted`, a payload none of whose hops started for want of budget among them;

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Security Audit Scope Analysis
# Two-Pass Methodology v1.0
#
# Shows file counts by security-relevant category to understand audit surface.
# Part of Loa's /audit skill enhancement.
#
# Usage: .claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh [OPTIONS]
#   --no-symlinks    Skip symlinks (default: follow)
#   --max-depth N    Limit search depth (default: unlimited)
#   --json           Output as JSON

set -euo pipefail

# Parse arguments
FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=true
MAX_DEPTH=""
OUTPUT_JSON=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case $1 in
    --no-symlinks) FOLLOW_SYMLINKS=false; shift ;;
    --max-depth) MAX_DEPTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json) OUTPUT_JSON=true; shift ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# Build find options as array (HIGH-002 remediation - prevents word splitting)
declare -a FIND_OPTS=(-type f)
if [[ "$FOLLOW_SYMLINKS" == "false" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-type f -not -type l)
fi
if [[ -n "$MAX_DEPTH" ]]; then
  FIND_OPTS=(-maxdepth "$MAX_DEPTH" "${FIND_OPTS[@]}")
fi

# Exclude patterns (POSIX compatible)
EXCLUDE_DIRS="node_modules|\.git|dist|build|\.next|vendor|__pycache__|\.venv"

# Count function with error suppression
# Uses array expansion for safe variable handling
count_files() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*.ts" -o -name "*.js" -o -name "*.py" -o -name "*.go" -o -name "*.java" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | \
    xargs grep -l "$pattern" 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

count_by_name() {
  local pattern="$1"
  local result
  result=$(find . "${FIND_OPTS[@]}" \( -name "*$pattern*" \) 2>/dev/null | \
    grep -v -E "$EXCLUDE_DIRS" | wc -l || echo "0")
  echo "$result" | tr -d '[:space:]'
}

     2	"""hop-locality.py — classify model hops as local or hosted for `hounfour.locality: local_voices` (cycle-129 FR-8,
     3	SDD D-8.0 / D-8.1, DEC-0146).
     4	
     5	    python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog <model-config.yaml> --config <.loa.config.yaml> -- <hop>...
     6	
     7	One tab-separated line per hop, in the order given:
     8	
     9	    <hop> TAB <provider|unknown> TAB <local|hosted> TAB <reason>
    10	
    11	A hop is `local` only when ALL of these hold in the merged view (the System Zone catalog overlaid with the project
    12	config's `hounfour.providers` / `hounfour.aliases`, the two layers cheval merges):
    13	  * it resolves (a `provider:id` pin, an alias chain, or a bare id that exactly one provider declares) to a model entry
    14	    that exists;
    15	  * that model entry, or its provider block, says `dispatch_group: local` (the canonical key, D-8.0);
    16	  * every hop on the entry's own `fallback_chain` is local by the same rule — cheval walks that chain inside one call,
    17	    so a local entry that falls back to a hosted one would leave the declared providers without the planner seeing it.
    18	Everything else is `hosted`: an unresolved hop, an unreadable config, a headless CLI hop (its dispatch group is the
    19	provider family's), the native session. Fail closed — a hop is never called local because it could not be read.
    20	
    21	This file reads declarations only: it never dispatches, never reads credentials and never imports the cheval package
    22	(run under `-I`, so neither the cwd nor PYTHONPATH reaches sys.path). The request-time rules for a local hop (IP-literal
    23	or localhost endpoint, no DNS, redirects refused, proxy env ignored, destination logged) are cheval's.
    24	"""

    26	
    27	import argparse
    28	import sys
    29	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
    30	
    31	MAX_DEPTH = 10

    34	def _merge(base: Any, overlay: Any) -> Any:
    35	    if isinstance(base, dict) and isinstance(overlay, dict):
    36	        out = dict(base)
    37	        for key, value in overlay.items():
    38	            out[key] = _merge(base.get(key), value) if key in base else value
    39	        return out
    40	    return overlay

    43	def load_merged(catalog_path: str, config_path: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    44	    import yaml
    45	
    46	    with open(catalog_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    47	        catalog = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}

    49	        raise ValueError("catalog is not a mapping")
    50	    merged: Dict[str, Any] = {k: (catalog.get(k) if isinstance(catalog.get(k), dict) else {})
    51	                              for k in ("providers", "aliases", "backward_compat_aliases")}

### DISS-C-001 [MEDIUM] secrets — .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:OpenAIAdapter.complete:172
The insecure-endpoint opt-in is independent of `keyless`. A provider configured with `allow_insecure_endpoint: 192.168.1.20`, `endpoint: http://192.168.1.20:8080/v1` and `auth: "{env:OPENAI_API_KEY}"` passes load-time validation, and the adapter sends the resolved API key as a Bearer header over plaintext HTTP (LAN sniffable, logged by any intermediate reverse proxy). The policy module's docstring frames the opt-in as 'a provider that needs no credential', but nothing enforces that coupling.
FAILURE: A hosted-vendor API key is transmitted in cleartext to an RFC1918 host (e.g. a LAN gateway or a mis-pointed proxy), exposing the credential to anyone on the network path.
FIX: In validate_providers, refuse (or at minimum WARN loudly) when `allow_insecure_endpoint` is set on a provider that is not `keyless: true`, or whose `auth` resolves to a non-empty value. Alternatively, have the adapter refuse to attach an Authorization header when the request URL scheme is http.

### DISS-C-002 [MEDIUM] input-validation — .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:OpenAIAdapter.complete:193
Structured-output enforcement can be downgraded by the remote server. `_names_response_format` treats ANY HTTP 400 whose body contains the substrings `response_format` or `json_schema` (any field, any case) as a schema rejection, and `complete` then re-sends the full prompt once without `response_format`. A hostile or compromised OpenAI-compatible server (the local/third-party servers this cycle is adding support for) can therefore (a) force every request to be sent twice, and (b) strip the strict schema so the tolerant parser / repair loop accepts arbitrary output. The heuristic also fires if the server echoes user-controlled prompt text containing those words in an unrelated 400 error, silently dropping schema enforcement on the retry.
FAILURE: Schema-constrained verdict calls run unenforced at the server's discretion; the prompt (possibly containing sensitive context) is transmitted twice; telemetry records it but the caller's output contract is weakened without an explicit operator decision.
FIX: Narrow the detection to the server's structured error object (e.g. `error.param == 'response_format'` or `error.code` naming unsupported_parameter) rather than a substring scan of the whole body. Consider making the schema-less retry opt-in per model (catalog flag) and surfacing `schema_rejected_by_server` to the caller as a degraded result instead of only to MODELINV.

### DISS-C-003 [MEDIUM] authz — .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/loader.py:load_config:704
Under `hounfour.locality: local_voices`, a `dispatch_group: local` model whose `fallback_chain` names a hosted hop is supposed to be refused at load (validate_local_fallbacks). Based on the diff shown, `load_config` never calls it, so the guarantee that a local-voices run keeps the prompt on-box is not enforced: cheval walks the fallback chain inside one call and would send the prompt to the hosted provider after a local failure (context_window_refused, timeout, 5xx). Could not verify whether another call site exists outside the reviewed hunks.
FAILURE: A prompt intended for a local model under local_voices locality is forwarded to a hosted vendor on fallback, violating the data-locality policy the operator configured.
FIX: Call `validate_local_fallbacks(merged)` immediately after `validate_providers(merged)` in load_config, and add a loader test that a local_voices config with a hosted fallback fails with CONFIG-INVALID.

### DISS-C-004 [MEDIUM] other — .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:hop_locality_of:473
MODELINV `hop_locality` is derived from the raw `dispatch_group == 'local'` label on the model entry. It ignores the provider-block label (which hop_is_local honours), the CLI exclusion, and the endpoint-host check. Two concrete divergences: (1) a provider with `dispatch_group: local` on the provider block is recorded as `hosted` in the audit chain while the planner treats it as local; (2) if `hop_telemetry` is ever fed a hounfour dict that did not pass through load_config (hand-built or stale), a hosted endpoint labelled `local` is recorded as `local`. The audit record is the artifact used to prove data locality after the fact.
FAILURE: The tamper-evident MODELINV chain can assert a locality that differs from what the dispatcher actually did, undermining audit/compliance review of local-vs-hosted routing.
FIX: Have hop_locality_of delegate to `endpoint_policy.hop_is_local(hounfour, provider, model_id)` (returning 'local'/'hosted'), so audit and dispatch share one implementation.

### DISS-C-005 [MEDIUM] secrets — .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:check_endpoint:?
The new Python load-time gate admits any public https host for any provider. Because `.loa.config.yaml` is a project-level file (overlaying `hounfour.providers`), a cloned repository can set e.g. `providers.openai.endpoint: https://attacker.example/v1` while keeping `auth: "{env:OPENAI_API_KEY}"`; cheval will then send the operator's real key as a Bearer header to the attacker's host. This is pre-existing on the Python path, but this change is the point where the Python side formalises endpoint policy and explicitly chooses to omit the control the bash path has.
FAILURE: Credential exfiltration via a malicious or tampered project config pointing a credentialed provider at a third-party https host.
FIX: Apply the canonical host allowlist (or a per-provider-type expected-host suffix) for providers whose `auth` is an `{env:...}` reference, allowing overrides only from the user/system config layer, not the project layer; at minimum WARN on load when a credentialed provider's host is not on the allowlist.

### DISS-C-006 [LOW] config — .claude/adapters/cheval.py:_build_provider_config:551
The adapter-side re-check only runs when `allow_insecure_endpoint` is present. A hand-built or stale config (the case the comment says this re-check exists for) with a plain `http://` or loopback/metadata endpoint and no opt-in is passed to ProviderConfig unchecked, relying entirely on load_config having run. Also, when an opt-in is present but `endpoint` is empty, the opt-in value itself is not validated here.
FAILURE: Defense-in-depth gap: configs that bypass load_config reach the transport with unvalidated endpoints.
FIX: Call `check_endpoint(endpoint, _optin_raw, provider_name)` unconditionally for non-CLI providers with a non-empty endpoint (it returns None when there is no opt-in), and validate a lone opt-in via canonical_optin_host.

### DISS-C-007 [LOW] info-disclosure — .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:describe_provider:?
describe-provider prints the post-interpolation `endpoint` verbatim to stdout (consumed by model-health-probe.sh). The docstring claims it never carries a secret, but an endpoint that embeds an interpolated value (e.g. a gateway token or tenant id in the URL path/query) is emitted as-is. The `_main` error path also prints `str(exc)` for interpolation failures, which can include the offending value.
FAILURE: Secrets embedded in endpoint templates leak into probe logs/CI output.
FIX: Emit only `split_url` scheme/host/port (as destination_for does) rather than the full endpoint, and route load errors through redact_config before printing.

content.content:
# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

===OUTSCHEMA
# Structured Finding Output Schema

Defines the JSONL output format for machine-parseable audit findings.

## Finding Schema

Each finding is a JSON object on a single line in the JSONL file.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "AuditFinding",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "category", "criterion", "severity", "score", "finding", "reasoning_trace", "confidence"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}$",
      "description": "Unique finding ID (e.g., SEC-001, ARCH-042)"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["security", "architecture", "code_quality", "devops", "blockchain"],
      "description": "Audit category"
    },
    "criterion": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Specific rubric dimension (e.g., input_validation, modularity)"
    },
    "severity": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["CRITICAL", "HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW", "INFO"],
      "description": "Finding severity"
    },
    "score": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 5,
      "description": "Rubric score for this dimension"
    },
    "file": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "File path where issue was found"
    },
    "line": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Line number (if applicable)"
    },
    "code_snippet": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Relevant code excerpt"
    },
    "reasoning_trace": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "How the issue was discovered - analysis path and evidence"
    },
    "finding": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Clear description of the issue"
    },
    "critique": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Specific guidance for improvement"
    },
    "remediation": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Exact fix with code example if applicable"
    },
    "confidence": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["high", "medium", "low"],
      "description": "Confidence in the finding"
    },
    "references": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {"type": "string"},
      "description": "CVE, CWE, OWASP, or other references"
    }
  }
}

# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md (Task 1.1: the change in `pr/head.diff` — sprint-257, cycle-129)
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= `pr/PR.md`)
**Task:** review-r21

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Executive Summary

The change adds a per-provider insecure-endpoint opt-in with request-time transport rules, keyless local providers, structured output and thinking-trace handling on the OpenAI-compatible chat path, advisory dissent voices, a `hounfour.locality: local_voices` posture across four consumers, a trusted-configuration layer for Bridgebuilder on pull requests, and exit code 3 for a degraded Bridgebuilder consensus. The security engineering is mostly careful: one endpoint rule in `endpoint-validator.py` reused by cheval, the bash wrapper and the probe; the opt-in grammar refuses DNS names, link-local, metadata and ULA addresses; the `TransportPolicy` disables proxy env and refuses redirects on both httpx and urllib; subprocess calls use argv (`execFileSync`, `python3 -I … --`); jq receives data via `--arg`/`--slurpfile`; hop names are regex-validated before they reach any command line; `isSafeRefName` guards `git show`; keyless providers put no placeholder credential on the wire.

The verdict turns on the posture feature. `local_voices` is a confidentiality guarantee, and Bridgebuilder's classifier admits a hop the PR's own classifier refuses: a local model whose `fallback_chain` names a hosted provider is kept, and cheval walks that chain inside the call. One HIGH forces CHANGES_REQUIRED under the one-way rule. Two MEDIUMs: the request-time rules are wired into one adapter family while the loader accepts the opt-in for every provider type, and the trusted-configuration layer protects keyless/insecure/locality/exit keys but not the `endpoint`/`auth` that cheval reads from the (attacker-controlled) head checkout, so the layer's stated threat model is only partly covered. Eight LOWs follow.

Prerequisite note: Phase 0 requires `engineer-feedback.md` to say "All good"; it says CHANGES REQUIRED (1 HIGH). The task brief directs the audit to run regardless, so it ran with that deviation recorded here. `grimoires/loa/known-failures.md` is absent (KF-SURFACE warning); triage proceeded without it. `.loa.config.yaml` has no `integrity_enforcement` key; no System-Zone drift check was possible or needed (the diff is read from `pr/`, nothing under `.claude/` was edited).

Scope limits: findings were confirmed by reading the `pr/head/` files and by reproductions recorded in the review; I did not re-run the pytest or bats suites (the review recorded 123 pytest / 45 bats passing on a hybrid tree), and the Bridgebuilder TypeScript tests could not be run (no `node_modules`; `dist/` hashes were verified against sources by the review).

**Security Issues Found:**
| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 8 |

---

## Critical Security Issues (Must Fix)

None.

---

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] Bridgebuilder's `local_voices` check ignores a local model's `fallback_chain`

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: medium) — Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-003 names the same chain walk)
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726` (`isLocalVoice`), `:739` (`applyLocality`), applied at `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/main.ts:486`
**Issue:** `isLocalVoice` decides from `dispatch_group` alone:
```ts
if (Object.hasOwn(decl.modelGroups, modelId) && decl.modelGroups[modelId] !== undefined) return decl.modelGroups[modelId] === "local";
if (decl.dispatchGroup !== undefined) return decl.dispatchGroup === "local";
```
The PR's classifier for the dissent and Flatline states the rule the posture needs — `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:16`: "every hop on the entry's own `fallback_chain` is local by the same rule — cheval walks that chain inside one call" — and returns `hosted` with `fallback_chain_reaches_hosted:<hop>` at `:133` (pinned by bats LOC-7). Bridgebuilder has no equivalent, and `ProviderDecl` (`core/types.ts`) does not even carry the chain. Every Bridgebuilder voice dispatches through cheval (`cheval-delegate.ts` passes `--model provider:model`), and cheval's `chain_resolver.py:92` appends the primary entry's `fallback_chain` to the walk.
**Scenario:** trusted config `hounfour.locality: local_voices`; provider `lan` with model `qwen` `dispatch_group: local`, `fallback_chain: ["openai:gpt-5.5"]`; multi-model voice `lan/qwen`. `applyLocality` keeps the voice. The local server times out or returns 5xx; cheval falls to `openai:gpt-5.5` and the PR diff plus prompt leave the host. `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:163-166` promises the voice is "dropped … and never rerouted"; `head/README.md:30` promises the posture "refuses every hosted hop by name across the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and the probe".
**Impact:** Confidentiality posture breach for one of four consumers, invisible to the operator (Bridgebuilder prints no refusal; cheval's MODELINV row records the hosted destination after the fact).
**Fix:** Parse `models.<id>.fallback_chain` into `ProviderDecl` and make `isLocalVoice` recurse over the chain against the trusted declarations plus `GENERATED_MODEL_REGISTRY` (any unresolved or non-local hop ⇒ hosted; depth-bounded like `MAX_DEPTH`), or shell out to `hop-locality.py` with the trusted config text. Add a `trusted-config.test.ts` case mirroring LOC-7 (`qwen-leaky` with a hosted chain is refused by name) and one for an undeclared chain hop.
**Reference:** CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html; OWASP A04:2021 Insecure Design — https://owasp.org/Top10/A04_2021-Insecure_Design/

---

## Medium Priority Security Issues

### [MED-001] Request-time transport rules apply to the OpenAI adapter family only

**Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high) — Confirmed by cross-model review (review-gate DISS-C-004 earlier today; the audit dissent did not repeat it)
**File:** `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:217-222` (`_transport_policy`); `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:153-156` (`validate_providers`); `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/base.py:270`, `:378`, `:468` (`policy` optional, default `None`)
**Issue:** `endpoint_policy.py:26-28` promises that "for an opted-in provider, or a model whose `dispatch_group` is `local`, the adapter ignores proxy environment variables, refuses HTTP redirects and requires every request URL to stay under the declared endpoint path". `TransportPolicy` is built in exactly one place:
```python
if getattr(self.config, "allow_insecure_endpoint", None) or getattr(model_config, "dispatch_group", None) == "local":
    return TransportPolicy(endpoint=self.config.endpoint, provider=self.provider)
```
`validate_providers` accepts `allow_insecure_endpoint` for any provider that is not a CLI provider (`_is_cli_provider`), regardless of `type`. `anthropic_adapter.py` and `google_adapter.py` (not in the diff) call `http_post`, `http_post_stream` and `http_get` without `policy`. The review reproduced a `type: anthropic` provider with `endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:9100/v1`, `keyless: true`, `allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"` loading cleanly. `hop-locality.py` is likewise provider-type-agnostic, so such a hop is planned as local under `local_voices` and dispatched with proxy env honoured and the urllib fallback following redirects.
**Fix:** Fail closed at load — refuse the opt-in and `dispatch_group: local` for provider types whose adapter does not implement the policy, with a named reason — or construct the policy in `ProviderAdapter` so every adapter type inherits it (and apply it in `health_check` for `dispatch_group: local` providers, which today get it only with an opt-in, `openai_adapter.py:858`). Add a load test for the refused shape.
**Reference:** CWE-693 Protection Mechanism Failure — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html

### [MED-002] Trusted configuration does not cover the `endpoint`/`auth` that cheval reads from the head checkout

**Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: medium) — pre-existing exposure; the new mitigation leaves it open. Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-005 raised the omitted allowlist on the Python path)
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:669-692` (head-only refusal), `:393-398` (`validateApiKeys`); `head/.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py:1291-1297` (`_declared_endpoint` skips the host allowlist); `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/loader.py:704`; claim at `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117-118` and `head/README.md:30`
**Issue:** The layer's own comment names the threat — `config.ts:669`: "on a PR the head checkout is attacker-controlled".
